newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Utel net 1996 profit $27.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Utel net 1996 profit $27.4 mln.

text.p: Utel, a Ukrainian- and foreign-owned telephone company which installs and operates long distance exchanges, reported net profits of $27.4 million for 1996, a company statement said on Tuesday.
"I can say 1996 was a banner year for Utel. We are reporting profits of over $27 million," said company president Stewart Reich at a news conference.

The company will begin paying tax this year, at the end of a five-year tax holiday.
Utel plans to install an international exchange in the western city of Lviv this year and another exchange serving former Soviet countries in the eastern city of Kharkiv in 1998, Reich said.
Utel is a joint-venture owned 51 percent by state concern Ukrtelekom, 19.5 percent by AT&T, 19.5 percent by Deutsche Telekom AG, and 10 percent by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (Dutch PTT).
